title: Themes
text:
theme() takes a preset and individual options. The presets follow ggplot2’s complete themes:



Preset
Look




vega
Vega-Lite’s defaults


gray (also grey, ggplot2)
gray panel with white grid lines


bw
white panel with a dark border and light grid


minimal
light grid, no border, and no axis lines


classic
axis lines and no grid


light
light gray border and grid


dark
dark background


void
no axes or grid



baseSize: scales every font size, with ggplot2’s proportions. Themes are written into the specification as Vega-Lite config, so HTML and static exports look the same.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('gray', baseSize: 12);

The individual options are font, legendPosition (right, left, top, bottom, or none), background, panelBackground, panelBorder, grid, titleAnchor, and padding. config: accepts raw Vega-Lite config, merged last. Calls without a preset build on the current theme.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('minimal', legendPosition: 'bottom', font: 'Georgia, serif', config: ['axis' => ['labelColor' => '#666666']])
    ->labs(title: 'A minimal theme with the legend below');

A page can also choose a theme at render time. The vega-embed option theme accepts the vega-themes names, and phiz adds 'auto', which follows the reader’s light or dark mode preference:
$plot->embed(['theme' => 'auto']);

title: Scales, coordinates, and labels
text:
scaleX(), scaleY(), scaleColor(), scaleFill(), scaleSize(), scaleShape(), scaleOpacity(), and scaleLinetype() configure the scale and guide for one aesthetic. Successive calls for the same aesthetic merge.
Scale options are passed to the Vega-Lite scale:

type: linear, log, sqrt, pow, symlog, time, ordinal, quantile, quantize, or threshold
domain and range
scheme, a Vega color scheme such as viridis, blues, set2, or tableau10
values, a manual palette as a level-to-value map or a list in level order
zero, nice, reverse, clamp, base, exponent, domainMid, and padding

Guide options are passed to the axis or legend:

name, the title
breaks, the tick or legend values
format, a d3 number or time format
labels, a Vega label expression
guide: false, which hides the axis or legend

use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::economics())
    ->aes(x: 'pop', y: 'pce')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)
    ->scaleY(type: 'log', breaks: [500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000], name: 'Personal consumption ($bn, log scale)')
    ->scaleX(format: '.3s', name: 'Population (thousands)');

use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(size: 40)
    ->scaleColor(values: ['f' => '#1B9E77', 'r' => '#7570B3', '4' => '#D95F02'], name: 'Drive');

Continuous position scales fit the data as in ggplot2: points and lines do not force the axis to include zero. Plots with bars, areas, histograms, or densities keep zero, since their lengths are measured from it. zero: true restores Vega-Lite’s default for a single scale.
The functions in Phiz\ include ggplot2’s common shortcuts, such as scale_x_log10(), scale_y_reverse(), scale_color_manual(), scale_fill_viridis(), scale_color_brewer(), scale_color_gradient(), and scale_color_gradient2().

text:
Output
A plot compiles to a Vega-Lite specification on demand.
$plot->toArray();        // the specification as a PHP array
$plot->toJson();         // as JSON
$plot->embed();          // an HTML fragment with the container and script tags
$plot->html();           // a standalone HTML page
$plot->svg();            // SVG through vl-convert
$plot->save('plot.pdf'); // the file extension picks the format
Rendering covers the options for each output, and Laravel and Livewire covers the Blade component.

title: Facets and composition
Facets and composition
Facets and composition
Design
text:
phiz does not draw graphics. It translates a ggplot2-style description into a Vega-Lite specification. Vega-Lite then resolves scales, lays out facets and legends, runs transforms, handles interaction, and renders to canvas or SVG. The PHP side stays small, and plots behave the same in the browser and in static export.
Most statistics run where Vega-Lite runs them: bins, densities, loess fits, aggregates, quantiles, and window functions are Vega-Lite transforms. phiz computes a statistic in PHP only when Vega-Lite cannot:

the confidence bands of smooth() with lm, quad, or poly
curve() evaluations of PHP functions
the bandwidth behind density(adjust:)
the statistics helpers’ intervals and predictions

title: Design
text:
Differences from ggplot2

bins: is a maximum, and Vega-Lite picks rounded bin boundaries. Use binwidth: for exact widths.
xlim() and ylim() zoom without removing data.
The default density bandwidth is Vega-Lite’s (Scott’s rule). adjust: uses R’s bw.nrd0 rule.
Loess smoothing uses Vega-Lite’s loess transform without a confidence band.
size on points is an area in square pixels, as in Vega-Lite, rather than a diameter in millimeters.
A discrete axis is 300 pixels by default and grows by 20 pixels per level beyond 15 levels. Vega-Lite’s own default is 20 pixels per level.
There is no violin geom. Vega-Lite cannot draw a density inside each band of a discrete axis, so violins could not share an axis with boxplots or points.
Default colors are Vega-Lite’s. theme('gray') gives ggplot2’s panel and grid but keeps Vega-Lite’s categorical palette.

title: Design
text:
Versions
phiz emits Vega-Lite 6 specifications. The pinned browser libraries are vega 6.4.0, vega-lite 6.4.3, and vega-embed 7.3.0. Static export uses vl-convert with Vega-Lite 6.1, and the tests validate every specification against the Vega-Lite 6.1.0 JSON schema, the version both renderers support.

title: Data and fields
text:
Plot::of() and each geom’s data: argument accept data in several shapes:

a list of row arrays, such as [['x' => 1, 'y' => 2], ...]
an array of equal-length columns, such as ['x' => [1, 2], 'y' => [2, 3]]
a phibble table, or any object with toRows() or toColumns()
a Laravel Collection, or any object with toArray()
any iterable of rows, where rows may be arrays or objects
Data::url('cars.csv'), which Vega-Lite fetches in the browser
Data::named('live'), a data source the page supplies at runtime

Inline data is embedded in the specification. Values are made safe for JSON: DateTimeInterface values become ISO 8601 strings, enums become their values, and NAN and INF become null, which Vega-Lite treats as missing.
use Phiz\Plot;

$columns = [
    'month' => ['2026-01-01', '2026-02-01', '2026-03-01', '2026-04-01', '2026-05-01', '2026-06-01'],
    'visits' => [1200, 1350, 1290, 1610, 1820, 1765],
];

$plot = Plot::of($columns)
    ->aes(x: 'month', y: 'visits')
    ->line()
    ->point(size: 50);

title: Data and fields
text:
Field types
Vega-Lite needs a measurement type for every mapped field. phiz infers it from inline data:

quantitative, when every non-null value is an integer or a float
temporal, when every value is an ISO date or date-time string
nominal, otherwise

A numeric code such as a cylinder count is quantitative by this rule. It gets a continuous color scale and gradient legend unless you mark it as categorical. Field shorthand sets the type explicitly with a suffix: :Q (quantitative), :N (nominal), :O (ordinal), or :T (temporal). factor('cyl') is the equivalent of R’s factor(cyl), and its levels: argument sets the order.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\factor;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mtcars())
    ->aes(x: 'wt', y: 'mpg', color: factor('cyl'), shape: 'am:N')
    ->point(size: 60)
    ->labs(color: 'Cylinders', shape: 'Manual');

URL data cannot be inspected in PHP, so phiz assumes quantitative positions and nominal groupings. Use shorthand types for anything else.

title: Data and fields
Data and fields
Data and fields
text:
Field definitions
field() builds a Field with any Vega-Lite field-definition property, such as field('date', timeUnit: 'month', title: 'Month') or field('term', sort: ['b', 'a', 'c']). A raw array is also accepted for any aesthetic and is used as given.
Field names containing dots or brackets, such as R’s Sepal.Length, are escaped automatically. Vega-Lite would otherwise read them as nested access.

title: Development
text:
composer test
The suite runs with Pest and covers several layers:

Spec snapshots for every geom, feature, statistics helper, and gallery example, in tests/.pest/snapshots/. After an intended change, run vendor/bin/pest --update-snapshots and review the diff.
Validation of every specification against the pinned Vega-Lite 6.1.0 JSON schema in tests/fixtures/.
Numerical checks of quantiles, least squares, smoothing bands, and predictions against values from R.
Blade component tests on Orchestra Testbench.
When vl-convert is available, a render of every gallery example to SVG. Some specifications pass the schema but fail to compile, and this smoke test catches them.

Tests that need the php_stats extension skip when it is not loaded. The saved fits in tests/fixtures/fits.json cover the rest.

Gallery

The gallery writes an HTML page of every example in examples/catalog.php, with each example’s code. The catalog is a plain PHP array, so other projects can reuse it.

title: Development
text:
Documentation
The documentation is a Quarto website in docs/. The pages include generated fragments for their examples:

Each file in docs/examples/ returns a chart.
php scripts/docs-examples.php runs every example. For each one it writes the code and the resulting specification to docs/_generated/, and an SVG to docs/figures/. It also copies the gallery.
quarto render docs builds the site into docs/_site/.
scripts/render-docs runs steps 2 and 3, then copies the site into docs/ for GitHub Pages.

title: Geoms
text:
Each geom adds a layer. Every geom method accepts these common arguments:
As in ggplot2, color is the outline of bars, areas, and tiles, and fill is their interior. For points, lines, and text, color is the main color. linetype accepts ggplot2’s names (dashed, dotted, dotdash, longdash, twodash), hex dash strings such as '44', or a dash array.

title: Geoms
Geoms
Geoms
Geoms
text:
Intervals
errorbar(), linerange(), and pointrange() draw intervals from ymin to ymax. With xmin and xmax they are horizontal. position: 'dodge' places groups side by side, which the coefficient plots use to compare models.
use Phiz\Plot;

$estimates = [
    ['site' => 'North', 'mean' => 4.1, 'lower' => 3.2, 'upper' => 5.0],
    ['site' => 'East', 'mean' => 5.3, 'lower' => 4.6, 'upper' => 6.1],
    ['site' => 'South', 'mean' => 3.4, 'lower' => 2.1, 'upper' => 4.6],
    ['site' => 'West', 'mean' => 4.8, 'lower' => 4.2, 'upper' => 5.5],
];

$plot = Plot::of($estimates)
    ->aes(x: 'site', y: 'mean', ymin: 'lower', ymax: 'upper')
    ->errorbar(width: 10)
    ->point(size: 60)
    ->hline(4.5, linetype: 'dashed', color: '#888888')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Mean score (95% CI)');

title: Geoms
text:
Reference lines
hline() and vline() draw rules at fixed values, at every value of a list, or at a mapped yintercept or xintercept field. abline() draws y = intercept + slope * x across the range of the data.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)
    ->abline(0, 1, linetype: 'dashed')
    ->hline(30, color: '#D62728')
    ->vline(20, color: '#1F77B4')
    ->labs(x: 'City mpg', y: 'Highway mpg');

title: Geoms
Geoms
Geoms
text:
Raw layers
layer() adds any Vega-Lite layer as given, and geom() adds a geom by name with explicit parameter and style arrays.

title: phiz
text:
phiz builds Vega-Lite specifications from PHP with a grammar modeled on ggplot2. Vega-Lite handles the layout, scales, interaction, and rendering. PHP code describes the plot, and you write no JavaScript. The same specification renders in the browser through vega-embed, or to SVG, PNG, or PDF through the vl-convert binary for reports and email.
Every chart on this site was produced by running the code shown above it. The examples live in docs/examples/, and scripts/docs-examples.php runs them and embeds the specifications they returned.

title: phiz
text:
Install
composer require erikwestlund/phiz
phiz requires PHP 8.5 and has no other dependencies. Static export needs the vl-convert binary. Laravel support is optional and is discovered automatically.

title: phiz
text:
What phiz covers

A fluent, immutable Plot builder, and ggplot2-style functions for PHP’s pipe operator.
About 30 geoms, including points, lines, areas, bars, histograms, densities, boxplots, intervals, reference lines, text, heatmaps, smoothers, QQ plots, and arcs.
Scales, coordinate flips and limits, facets, compositions, labels, and themes modeled on ggplot2’s complete themes.
Tooltips, pan and zoom, brushing, legend highlighting, sliders, and linked views, all expressed as Vega-Lite parameters.
Statistical plots built from php-stats model results and CmdStanPHP draws: coefficient plots, regression diagnostics, predicted values with confidence bands, and posterior intervals.
HTML output, static export, and an <x-phiz> Blade component that re-renders inside Livewire.

title: phiz
text:
The phpstats family
phiz is the visualization package of the phpstats family. php-stats fits the models, phibble provides data frames, phplyr provides dplyr verbs, and CmdStanPHP runs Stan. phiz depends on none of them. It reads any of their tables directly.

title: Laravel and Livewire
text: phiz’s Laravel service provider is discovered automatically. It registers the <x-phiz> Blade component and the @phizScripts directive. Without Laravel, the same classes are never loaded.

title: Laravel and Livewire
text:
Blade
<x-phiz :plot="$plot" class="h-80" />
The component accepts a Plot, a Compose, a specification array, or specification JSON. :options passes vega-embed options, merged over config('phiz.embed_options'). Other attributes go to the container element.
The first <x-phiz> on a page adds the script tags. To place them yourself, put @phizScripts in the layout.

title: Rendering
text:
toArray() returns the Vega-Lite specification and toJson() encodes it. Plots also implement JsonSerializable. The specification declares the Vega-Lite 6 schema.
Four escape hatches reach the parts of Vega-Lite that phiz does not wrap:

raw([...]) deep-merges arbitrary Vega-Lite into the top level. Nested objects merge, and lists and scalars replace.
transform(...) adds Vega-Lite transforms that run before every layer.
layer([...]) adds a raw Vega-Lite layer.
param() and select() add raw parameters.

text:

title: Rendering
text:
HTML
embed() returns a container element followed by the script tags, and html() returns a standalone page. Both pass vega-embed options, such as ['actions' => false] or ['renderer' => 'svg'].
The container carries the specification in a data-phiz attribute. A small loader script, about 100 lines, renders every such element with vega-embed. It renders them again when the attribute changes. The same markup therefore works in static pages, Blade views, and Livewire components.
The browser libraries are pinned:



Library
Version




vega
6.4.0


vega-lite
6.4.3


vega-embed
7.3.0



Assets chooses where they come from:
use Phiz\Assets;

$plot->embed(assets: Assets::cdn());                 // jsDelivr, with subresource integrity (the default)
$plot->embed(assets: Assets::local('/js/vega'));     // copies you serve: vega.min.js, vega-lite.min.js, vega-embed.min.js
$plot->html(assets: Assets::inline('/path/to/js'));  // embedded in the page, for offline files
$plot->embed(assets: Assets::none());                // your bundle already sets window.vegaEmbed
$plot->embed(assets: false);                         // just the container

title: Rendering
Statistics
text:
The statistics helpers build ordinary plots from model results, so their output can be restyled with any Plot method. They read the arrays that php-stats returns. Formula fits from stats_lm, stats_glm, stats_lmer, and stats_glmer name their coefficients in columns. Matrix fits from stats_ols and stats_logistic take a names: argument.
The fits on this page were produced by php-stats from the mtcars data and saved in docs/examples/fits/.
